title: House Robber III
statement: Each tree node has a value; maximize the sum chosen without selecting both a node and its direct child.
explanation: For each subtree compute the best value when taking its root and when skipping it.

title: Counting Bits
statement: For every integer i from 0 through n, return the number of one bits in its binary representation.
explanation: The bit count of i equals the bit count of i>>1 plus its least significant bit.

title: Flatten Nested List Iterator
statement: Implement an iterator that returns all integers from a nested list in their left-to-right order.
explanation: Maintain iterators for nested lists and descend into a nested list when encountered.

title: Power of Four
statement: Determine whether a positive integer is an exact power of four.
explanation: A power of four has exactly one set bit and that bit is in an even-numbered position.

title: Integer Break
statement: Split integer n into at least two positive integers and maximize their product.
explanation: For n above the small cases, factors of three maximize the product; replace a remainder of one with two twos.

title: Reverse String
statement: Reverse an array of characters in place using constant extra space.
explanation: Swap the left and right characters and move the pointers toward the center.

title: Reverse Vowels of a String
statement: Return the string with only its vowels reversed while all other characters remain in their positions.
explanation: Move two pointers inward until both point at vowels, then swap them.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
statement: Return the k most frequent values in an integer array.
explanation: Count frequencies, bucket values by count, and collect from highest frequency downward.

title: Intersection of Two Arrays
statement: Return the distinct values that appear in both integer arrays.
explanation: Convert the arrays to sets and return their intersection.

title: Intersection of Two Arrays II
statement: Return the multiset intersection of two arrays, including each common value as many times as it appears in both.
explanation: Count values from one array and consume a count whenever a match is found in the other.
